Center on U.S.–China Relations

In seeking new ways of building mutual understanding between the United States and China, the Center undertakes projects and events which explore areas of common interest and divergent views between the two countries, focusing on policy, culture, business, media, economics, energy and the environment.

Task Force on U.S.-China Relations

Co-chaired by Orville Schell and Susan Shirk, the Task Force on U.S.-China Policy includes former U.S. government officials, scholars, and think tank researchers, many of whom served under both political parties and almost every U.S. president since the Nixon administration. The group analyzes and engages on issues in the bilateral relationship.

725 Salon

Recognizing the large and growing population of Mandarin Chinese speakers in New York, the Center's flagship Mandarin Chinese language event series features experts and thought leaders for discussions on issues pertaining to China, U.S.-China relations, and the experience of Chinese living in the United States.

Our Fellows

Based around the world, Center on U.S.-China Relations fellows contribute significant research in the areas of U.S.-China relations, journalism and new media, history, and the environment.
